preamble: Click loss by deletion of the front (dental) closure: the voiceless dental click [ǀ] keeps only its velar back closure and becomes [k]. The mechanism is phonetic (the front closure is lost, the velar kept), but Gunnink (2020, 2022) attributes the free variation in the border area to contact between the two varieties. Southern (Namibian) Fwe keeps clicks, and the clickless northern (Zambian) variety has velars in the same words; speakers in the border zone alternate freely (Gunnink 2022; Sands & Gunnink 2019). Prenasalized voiceless clicks likewise alternate with [ᵑk]. Sands & Gunnink (2019) link the loss to northern Fwe's contact with clickless Lozi, Kwamashi and Shanjo. They report similar replacement of clicks by velar non-clicks in Northern Ndebele (South Africa), where clicks were still used in some plant names in the 1950s but had been replaced by the 2000s; no Ndebele forms are cited there. For Mupa ǃXuun (Kx'a), alveolar clicks are said to be replaced by velar non-clicks (Fehn, cited in Sands & Gunnink 2019). In Yeyi, a voiced alveolar click in the Botswana variety corresponds to a non-click velar in the Namibian variety: kù-ì-ɡǃámánì vs kù-ì-khyàmínà 'to throw' (Sands & Gunnink 2019, ex. 5). That pair is not counted here.
phoneticEffects: Click Loss, Deletion Of Front Closure, Merger
